source_facts: ThreadGauge 2.4 is a synthetic textile inspection system. These facts are authoritative for the optical-triage guide on loom-6. The audience is mill support technicians investigating intermittent stripe alerts, not personnel authorizing fabric acceptance or loom restart. The loom must be stopped before either a diagnostic snapshot or a hood adjustment. The cloth guide must be locked before either action. These are separate prerequisites. The existing mill stop-and-lock procedure supplies those conditions; this page does not invent machine-control commands. Run `tgauge snapshot --loom loom-6 --out /var/tmp/stripe.json` to write a read-only diagnostic snapshot. The command neither restarts the loom nor changes its inspection baseline. The snapshot contains baseline_revision, glare_score, and stripe_count. The required baseline revision for this guide is B17. If the snapshot uses another revision, stop this triage and refer it to Quality Engineering; do not recalibrate as part of this guide. The baseline check precedes interpretation of the two scores. glare_score measures reflected-light interference on an integer scale from 0 through 100 inclusive. It does not measure how many fabric defects exist. A glare score of at least 70 takes the glare branch regardless of stripe_count. For that branch, fit the existing matte hood, then capture another snapshot under the same stop-and-lock prerequisites. If the new score remains at least 70, refer the optical problem to Quality Engineering rather than repeatedly adjusting the hood. Once a snapshot has glare_score below 70, use stripe_count. That field counts contiguous dark bands in the snapshot, not completed rolls of fabric. At least 3 bands under low glare require referral to Quality Engineering for textile assessment. Fewer than 3 bands under low glare allow closing the optical ticket as transient. Closing this ticket does not authorize loom restart or fabric release. Examples use a valid B17 snapshot: glare_score=82 with stripe_count=1 takes the hood branch; glare_score=24 with stripe_count=4 takes the textile-assessment branch. These examples are illustrative results, not required machine settings. Attach the final snapshot at /var/tmp/stripe.json to the optical ticket for either closure or referral. A recapture writes the current snapshot to the same example path, so the attachment is the final result. `mill-stop-lock.md` is the supplemental stop-and-lock procedure, `matte-hood.md` is the existing hood-fitting reference, and `quality-intake.md` is the Quality Engineering evidence-intake reference. Necessary branch conditions and meanings are supplied in this page. No baseline-edit, fabric-release, or restart procedure is within scope.

# ThreadGauge intermittent stripe alerts

This guide is for support technicians investigating intermittent stripe alerts on loom-6. It covers optical triage and the evidence passed to Quality Engineering. It does not authorize fabric release or loom restart. Use the optical ticket to keep the final diagnosis connected to the captured result.

## Close an optical ticket

Under low glare, fewer than 3 bands allow the optical ticket to be closed as transient. Closing that ticket is not permission to restart the loom or release fabric. Attach the final `/var/tmp/stripe.json` snapshot to the ticket when closing it so the next reader can see the result behind the decision.

## Two reported results

A B17 snapshot with `glare_score=82` and `stripe_count=1` takes the hood branch. Another B17 snapshot with `glare_score=24` and `stripe_count=4` goes to Quality Engineering for textile assessment. These are example observations, not values to enter into a machine setting. A technician should classify the captured result rather than trying to make it resemble either example.

## Capture evidence

Run `tgauge snapshot --loom loom-6 --out /var/tmp/stripe.json`. The snapshot is read-only: it does not change the inspection baseline or restart the loom. It reports `baseline_revision`, `glare_score`, and `stripe_count`. A second capture writes the current result to the same example path, leaving the final snapshot ready to attach.

## Optical correction

A glare score of at least 70 takes the glare branch regardless of the stripe count. Fit the existing matte hood using [Matte hood](matte-hood.md), then capture again. If the new glare score is still at least 70, refer the optical problem to Quality Engineering instead of repeatedly adjusting the hood.

## About bands

The `stripe_count` field counts contiguous dark bands in a snapshot. It is not a count of completed fabric rolls. Once glare is below 70, a count of at least 3 bands requires a textile-assessment referral to Quality Engineering. The evidence-intake details are in [Quality intake](quality-intake.md).

## Before touching the station

The loom must be stopped before either a diagnostic snapshot or a hood adjustment. The cloth guide must also be locked before either action. Obtain both conditions through the existing [Mill stop and lock](mill-stop-lock.md) procedure. They apply again when taking a snapshot after fitting the hood. This diagnostic guide does not introduce substitute machine-control commands.

## Check the baseline

Interpret the scores only after confirming `baseline_revision` is B17. Another revision means this guide is not applicable: stop this triage and refer the result to Quality Engineering. Do not recalibrate the inspection baseline as part of this workflow.

## Reflected light

The `glare_score` field measures reflected-light interference on an integer scale from 0 through 100, inclusive. It does not count defects in the cloth. A snapshot must have glare below 70 before its stripe count is used for the low-glare decision.

## Evidence for referrals

Attach the final `/var/tmp/stripe.json` to the optical ticket when referring either an unresolved optical problem or a low-glare textile concern. The two referrals have different reasons even though the intake team and evidence file are the same.

issues.description: Capture evidence and Optical correction appear before the stopped-loom and locked-guide prerequisites, while baseline applicability is introduced after the score-based branches.
issues.acceptable_resolution: Make physical readiness available before either action and baseline applicability available before score interpretation. Separate gates, a preflight, or clearly guarded branch entries are acceptable.

issues.description: The guide starts with ticket closure and then jumps through examples, capture, correction, meanings, and setup instead of presenting discoverable diagnostic decisions.
issues.acceptable_resolution: Provide an accessible symptom-to-disposition structure, such as a decision table, linked branches, or ordered diagnostic sections, without prescribing a single prose sequence.

issues.description: Low-glare interpretation is split between Close an optical ticket, About bands, and Reflected light, separating mutually exclusive outcomes from their shared condition.
issues.acceptable_resolution: Make the two low-glare outcomes and their common prerequisite usable together while retaining the distinct optical and textile referral reasons.

issues.description: The two numerical results are presented before either score is defined and without navigation to the branch rules that explain them.
